scope: Independent actual-daemon DNS requests in new network/mount/PID namespaces; exact OpenWrt image ELF versus fresh Rust ELF. No product changes or physical router access.

identities.shared_setup: m2_rootfs.py used only for exact-image identity checking, disposable read-only lower/overlay setup and chroot argv. Query construction, stub upstream, socket clients and comparisons are new.

summary.conclusion: No blocker identified by this DNS slice. Seven unsupported/malformed TCP request cases differ in error reporting, also present in the old baseline. Two unusual compression cases produce a defective exact-C reply and a valid re-encoded Rust reply.

findings.title: TCP closes on unsupported/malformed questions before reaching the implemented REFUSED reply path
findings.observed: Exact C returns QR/RA/REFUSED (0x8185). Rust closes that client connection without a DNS frame. Other clients remain healthy. The old main-equivalent ELF behaves identically to fresh Rust.

input_classification.multi-question: Two structurally encoded DNS questions; outside dnsmasq extract_request single-question interface. Not an ordinary supported request.
input_classification.multi-question-compressed: Same unsupported two-question shape using a backwards compression pointer in question 2.
input_classification.zero-question: Empty question section; no ordinary DNS lookup specified.
input_classification.outside-pointer: Invalid name: compression target outside received packet.
input_classification.bitstring-label: Obsolete extended label encoding unsupported by the request decoder.
input_classification.overlong-name: Invalid expanded name: 256 wire bytes, beyond its 255-byte bound.

source_path.observation: answer_query propagates that cache-view error before run_forward; caller retires connection.
query_error already constructs REFUSED for these inputs, but actual daemon caller does not reach it.
Exact C extract_request failure records invalid-data EDE and continues to make_local_answer at line 2733.

findings.impact_boundary: Low-impact compatibility difference on error inputs; not evidence of process DoS, supported lookup failure, security bypass, or a regression introduced by this branch. Whether to preserve C error-response behavior is a policy choice.

findings.title: Rust re-encodes an unusual forward-pointer question while C echoes a now-cyclic compressed question
findings.observed: Input question points to a name in trailing data at offset 18. C local answer discards the trailing name and writes its answer at offset 18: the question c012 points to answer owner c00c and loops. Rust expands the question and returns a decodable host A answer. This is not counted as a Rust defect.

limitations: Finite synthetic slice, not a protocol proof or exhaustive fuzzer.
368 paired cases count profile/transport/EDNS variants, not 368 unique semantic behaviors.
Forwarding uses a deterministic isolated stub upstream; no real resolver or WAN exercised.
cache-size=0 is intentional to avoid cached state contaminating pair comparisons; dynamic cache aging/coalescing/resend and resource pressure are outside this slice.
TCP queries use one frame per connection; pipelining and half-close behavior are outside this slice.
0.3-second no-response timeout bounds the harness; EOF witnesses are immediate connection termination rather than timeout.
Exact byte comparison intentionally exposes encoding differences; C-defective forward-pointer replies are classified separately.
